turns.text:
HTTP 304 means "Not Modified." The server sends it in reply to a conditional request, one that carries an `If-None-Match` header with an ETag or an `If-Modified-Since` header with a date. It tells the client that the resource hasn't changed since the version it already has cached, so the client can keep using that copy.

A 304 response has no body, which saves bandwidth. It can still include headers like `ETag`, `Cache-Control`, or `Expires` to refresh the cached entry's metadata. Strictly speaking it's a redirect-class (3xx) code, but in practice it just means "use your cache."
